Local Air Quality
The San Jose vicinity experiences high carbon monoxide (CO) levels resulting from the local motor vehicle source. High concentrations of nitrogen dioxide (NO<sub>2</sub>), oxidant, and reactive hydrocarbons result from sizeable regional emissions and stagnat air, rather than local conditions. The table below presents the maximum pollutant concentrations and number of violation days experienced at the San Jose air monitoring station over the past three years. Although hydrocarbon (HC) data is not shown in the table, the HC standard is exceeded almost every day in the Bay Area by a factor of ten or more (BAAPCD,1975). In contrast, the ambient sulfur dioxide (SO<sub>2</sub>) standard is almost never exceeded in the Bay Area or in San Jose.
